modules.name: bithuman
modules.doc:
bithuman — run an avatar on this machine.

    import bithuman
    avatar = bithuman.open("A63GVG1577.imx")
    for image in avatar.render(audio):
        show(image)

Two operations: **open an avatar, then render audio through it.**  Frames come
back as ``(height, width, 3)`` uint8 arrays in RGB order, at the avatar's own
frame rate.  ``audio`` is 16 kHz mono — a buffer, the path of an audio file, or
an iterable of buffers for a live stream; passing a stream instead of a whole
clip is the same call.

**Both families open the same way.**  essence-2 and expression-2 avatars are
the same two lines above; nothing in your code says which one you have.
expression-2 needs one extra package on this machine::

    pip install "bithuman[expression-2]"

Eight names, and that is the whole surface::

    open  ·  Avatar.render  ·  Avatar
    AvatarError  ·  InvalidAvatar  ·  NotSupported  ·  NotAuthorised  ·  Failed

There is nothing to configure.  This package runs the avatar on this machine,
in your process, so there is nothing left to choose about where or how it runs
— you chose that when you chose this package instead of the cloud one.

A key belongs in the environment, not in your code::

    export BITHUMAN_API_SECRET=...        # rendering is metered

**One command, if you would rather not write anything.**  Give it an avatar
and some audio and it writes a video::

    python -m bithuman A63GVG1577 speech.wav       # -> A63GVG1577.mp4

The avatar can be a ten-character code — it is fetched once, which is free —
or a file you already have.  Run it with no arguments to see the avatars your
key can open.

No audio to hand?  This package ships 15 s of speech at
``bithuman/assets/demo_sample.wav`` — ``python -m bithuman --help`` prints its
path on this machine.

★``pip install bithuman`` never puts a command on your PATH, and the line
above is why it does not have to.  That is an invariant, not an accident:
a pip-installed command named ``bithuman`` would overwrite the one Homebrew
puts at the same path, so ``tests/test_no_console_script.py`` fails if a
future release grows one.  ``python -m`` needs no script and cannot collide
with one.  The full command-line tool is still a separate artifact::

    curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bithuman-product/homebrew-bithuman/main/install.sh | sh

**Pinned to ``bithuman<3``?  This release still answers.**  2.11.0 carries
the complete 2.x import surface alongside the two operations above —
``AsyncBithuman``, ``Bithuman``, ``AudioChunk``, ``VideoFrame``,
``VideoControl``, the ``Fixture``/``Runtime`` handles and the 2.x exception
hierarchy all import and work::

    from bithuman import AsyncBithuman
    runtime = await AsyncBithuman.create(model_path="A63GVG1577.imx",
                                         api_secret="bh-...")

That is what keeps ``livekit-plugins-bithuman`` — which pins ``bithuman<3``
and imports ``AsyncBithuman`` — working with nothing to change.  The two
operations above are still the whole *taught* surface; the 2.x names are
carried for compatibility, not taught.  One name changed meaning and is
listed in the source below: ``Avatar`` is what ``open()`` returns, and 2.x's
synchronous ``Avatar`` is reachable as ``Bithuman``.

symbols.name: open
symbols.doc:
Open an avatar and return it.

``source`` is the avatar file on this machine.  This package runs the
avatar **here**, in your process; nothing is sent anywhere to make a
frame.

Raises :class:`InvalidAvatar` if it cannot be found or is not usable,
:class:`NotSupported` if it cannot run on this machine,
:class:`NotAuthorised` if the key is missing, invalid or out of credit,
and :class:`Failed` if something else went wrong.

symbols.name: Avatar
symbols.doc: An open avatar.  Get one from :func:`bithuman.open`.

members.name: render
members.doc:
Yield the frames for ``audio``.

``audio`` is 16 kHz mono — a buffer (bytes, or an int16/float array),
the path of an audio file, or an **iterable of those** for a live
stream.  Passing a stream instead of a whole clip is the same call.

Each frame is a ``(height, width, 3)`` uint8 array in RGB order.
Frames arrive in order, at the avatar's own frame rate — which is a
property of the avatar, not something to choose.

To stop early — a person interrupting the avatar — stop consuming and
close the iterator; the avatar is ready for the next ``render``.

symbols.name: InvalidAvatar
symbols.doc:
We cannot find it, or it is not a usable avatar.

Fix the path or the code, or fetch the avatar again.

symbols.name: NotSupported
symbols.doc:
This avatar cannot run here.

Render it in the cloud with the Video API (POST /v1/video/generate),
or open it on Apple Silicon macOS or Linux.

symbols.name: NotAuthorised
symbols.doc:
The key is missing, invalid, or out of credit.

Fix the credential.

symbols.name: Failed
symbols.doc:
We could not do it — transient, or our fault.

Retry, then report it.

symbols.name: Bithuman
symbols.doc:
High-level convenience wrapper around `Fixture` + `Runtime`.

Load a .imx once, then call `compose(audio)` to stream BGR frames.
Use as a context manager (or call `.close()`) to release the underlying
C handles deterministically.

symbols.name: AsyncBithuman
symbols.doc:
Async-first facade over libessence for parity with legacy
`bithuman.AsyncBithuman`. Construct via ``await AsyncAvatar.create(...)``.

NOTE (consolidation): this is the relocated *internal* native
facade, kept reachable so nothing Phase-1/2 is lost. The public,
canonical async class is ``bithuman.AsyncBithuman``
(``bithuman.runtime_async``); ``bithuman.AsyncAvatar`` is an alias
of THAT. The Phase-1/2 loader lives in
:class:`bithuman._loader.NativeFixtureLoaderMixin` (single
source of truth) and is inherited here AND by the canonical
``AsyncBithuman``.

Lifecycle:

    avatar = await AsyncAvatar.create(model_path=..., api_secret=...)
    await avatar.push_audio(pcm_bytes, sample_rate=16_000, last_chunk=True)
    async for frame in avatar.run():
        ...
    await avatar.shutdown()

symbols.name: ComposedFrame
symbols.doc:
One avatar frame produced by `Avatar.compose`.

Attributes
----------
bgr:
    (H, W, 3) uint8 numpy array in BGR pixel order. View into a buffer
    that the runtime may overwrite on the next tick; copy it if you
    need to retain the frame across iterations.
cluster_idx:
    The viseme cluster id chosen for this tick (range [0, cluster_count)).
frame_idx:
    Zero-based tick index inside the current compose() call.

symbols.name: EP
symbols.doc:
Execution provider hint. CPU is the canonical baseline; the others
are mapped opportunistically by the C ABI when available on the host.

symbols.name: AudioChunk
symbols.doc:
One chunk of audio bound for the avatar runtime.

Attributes
----------
data:
    Audio samples as a 1-D int16 numpy array. The constructor will
    coerce ``bytes`` / float32 / float64 input to int16 to match
    legacy semantics.
sample_rate:
    Sample rate in hertz (typically 16000 for the avatar pipeline).
last_chunk:
    Marks the final chunk of a speech utterance. The runtime uses
    this to flush internal buffers and emit ``end_of_speech`` on
    the final composed frame.

symbols.name: VideoControl
symbols.doc:
One unit of input to the avatar runtime.

The runtime consumes a stream of these. Each control is either
"speaking" (has an ``AudioChunk``), an action / target-video cue,
an emotion override, or "idle" (everything None) — in which case
the runtime emits idle-loop frames.

symbols.name: VideoFrame
symbols.doc:
One composed avatar frame.

Attributes
----------
bgr_image:
    (H, W, 3) uint8 BGR image, or None for control-only frames
    (e.g. end-of-speech markers without a render attached).
audio_chunk:
    The audio slice that aligns with this frame, or None if the
    runtime is in idle-loop / no-speech mode.
frame_index:
    Zero-based tick index inside the current speech utterance,
    reset whenever the runtime transitions speaking → idle.
source_message_id:
    Echoes the ``message_id`` of the originating VideoControl,
    so consumers can correlate frames back to the request.
end_of_speech:
    True only on the final composed frame of an utterance.

symbols.name: Emotion
symbols.doc:
Emotion label, matches legacy `bithuman.api.Emotion`.

These are the seven canonical labels the agent worker prompts the
LLM with. They flow through JSON as their string values.

symbols.name: EmotionPrediction
symbols.doc:
Emotion classifier output for one audio segment.

Legacy uses pydantic BaseModel with fields ``emotion`` + ``score``;
we use ``dataclass`` to avoid pulling in pydantic for the core
wrapper, while keeping the field names and serialization shape.

symbols.name: BithumanError
symbols.doc:
Base class for all bitHuman errors.

Carries a stable string `code` (e.g. "model_not_found") + a
`docs_url` pointing at the canonical docs page for that error.
Catch on this base for any bitHuman error, or on a specific
subclass for targeted handling.

symbols.name: Fixture
symbols.doc:
Loaded bitHuman avatar model (an .imx container) backed by the native libessence engine.

Low-level/advanced API: most callers should use the high-level ``bithuman.AsyncBithuman`` / ``bithuman.Bithuman``. A Fixture memory-maps the model once and exposes its immutable properties; pass it to ``Runtime`` to run inference. TAR-format console exports are auto-converted to v2 on load; legacy/encoder-less models use the process default encoder registered via ``set_default_audio_encoder``.

symbols.name: Runtime
symbols.doc:
Stateful inference session over a loaded ``Fixture``.

Low-level/advanced API (the high-level ``AsyncBithuman`` wraps this). Feed 25 fps audio ticks to ``tick`` for the cluster index, or ``tick_compose_to_size`` for a composed BGR frame. ``be_runtime_tick`` is metered — authenticate first via ``auth_init``/``auth_authenticate``.

symbols.name: libengine
symbols.doc:
libengine — Python binding over the be_engine_* narrow-waist C ABI.

A thin ctypes wrapper so a Python host (the `bithuman` wheel, tools, tests) can
drive the ONE engine — open a `.imx`, feed audio, pull frames, meter — regardless
of which engine/plane backend serves it. This is the Python arm of "one tool over
one waist" (ARCHITECTURE.md): the same be_engine_* contract the Rust CLI, the
Swift package, and the cloud worker speak.

Load the SHARED libengine (built with -DENGINE_BUILD_SHARED=ON, OUTPUT_NAME
`engine`). Backends are separate dlopen'd `.so`s resolved by the facade; set the
search dir with Engine.set_backend_search_dir().

    from libengine import LibEngine, HostCaps, Tier
    eng = LibEngine("/path/libengine.so")
    with eng.open("avatar.imx", host_caps=HostCaps(["coreml-neural-engine", "onnxruntime-cpu"], Tier.OFFLINE_PREPAID)) as sess:
        sess.feed_audio(pcm_int16_bytes)
        frame = sess.pull_frame()   # bytes, or None on an idle/not-ready poll

modules.name: bithuman.offline
modules.doc:
``bithuman.offline`` — the essence-2 self-hosted offline render.

    from bithuman.offline import OfflineRenderer, render_offline

    stats = render_offline("A63GVG1577.imx", "speech.wav", out_mp4="out.mp4")
    assert stats["borrow_state"] == "borrowed"

This is the reference route: it renders a whole clip on CPU through the same
pipeline the hosted engine runs, and every render says whether the avatar's own
teeth were used.  ``stats["borrow_state"]`` is one of the five ``BORROW_*``
names below and is the field to gate on; ``stats["borrow"]`` carries the
per-frame evidence behind it.

This module is not part of the eight-name taught surface (``bithuman.open`` and
``avatar.render`` are); it is kept for the callers that drive the offline route
directly.

★2.x SPELLINGS.  ``bithuman.tessera_offline`` (module), ``OfflineTesseraRenderer``
and ``TesseraOfflineError`` (classes) are the 2.x names of the things below.
Importing the old module warns and keeps working until 4.0.0.  The two 2.x
install extras are gone since 2.11.6: this route needs nothing beyond the base
wheel (and ffmpeg on PATH), and pip answers an extra a wheel does not declare
with a warning, rc=0 and the base install — which is the whole install.  The 2.x
stats key ``stats["tessera"]`` is gone — it is ``stats["borrow"]``.  The 2.x
``BITHUMAN_TESSERA_*`` / ``BITHUMAN_OFFLINE_*`` environment keys configured a
second, Python-side director this route no longer carries (2.11.5); nothing
reads them, and a program that sets them renders exactly as one that does not.

symbols.name: OfflineRenderer
symbols.doc:
Offline CPU renderer for an **essence-2** ``.imx``/bundle dir.
Metering is armed at CONSTRUCTION (billing key first); the teeth borrow is
armed at construction too, and an avatar that cannot borrow is refused
here, before any frame exists.

The model is called **essence-2** — that is the only name to write.
``essence2-light`` below is not a second product name: it is the
frozen ``engine`` literal stamped inside every essence-2 container,
read back off the file and compared here. It is a value you may READ
out of a bundle, never one you type.

modules.name: bithuman.tessera_offline
modules.doc:
DEPRECATED — the 2.x spelling of :mod:`bithuman.offline`.  Removed in 4.0.0.

Everything here is the same object as in ``bithuman.offline``; only the names
differ, and importing this module says so once::

    from bithuman.tessera_offline import OfflineTesseraRenderer   # 2.x
    from bithuman.offline import OfflineRenderer                  # 3.0.0

    OfflineTesseraRenderer is OfflineRenderer      # True
    TesseraOfflineError is OfflineRenderError      # True

★WHY THIS FILE EXISTS.  A customer's ``import`` and ``except`` resolve by exact
spelling against whatever version pip installed, and 34,636 installs a month
resolve this package unpinned.  A rename that deletes the old module turns an
upgrade into ``ModuleNotFoundError`` with no sentence about what to write
instead; a rename that keeps it, warns, and points at the new name is one a
program can act on.  ``tests/test_offline_alias_surface.py`` pins that the two
spellings are one object and that this module warns while the new one is silent.
